schema_description: first_run_controls_by_release lists the missing-model action for each release. can_defer applies only to that model's first-run path, not to later integrity retries, cache resets, or existing-install startup
privacy_model: Local dictation without Presspeech-authored analytics or cloud transcription; bundled-library network behavior varies by published version

network_calls.name: macos_first_launch_model_download
network_calls.when: macOS 0.3.8 starts its first model download on launch. In 0.3.9, a clean install without a complete model cache must choose Download Model in Setup; choosing Set Up Later defers the transfer. A complete preinstalled cache can load offline without granting future download permission; an incomplete cache needs the choice. Existing installs keep automatic startup. An integrity failure may redownload automatically only when download permission is already recorded; otherwise a clean install must reset the cache and choose Download Model first
destination: Hugging Face model-storage and CDN hosts under hf.co
macOS 0.3.8 and 0.3.9: inherited lowercase https_proxy and http_proxy settings can route HTTPS model requests through a configured HTTPS proxy
network_calls.purpose: FluidAudio downloads the Parakeet TDT v3 CoreML model weights
network_calls.proxy_preflight_by_release: In macOS 0.3.8, the pinned FluidAudio client may log a malformed inherited https_proxy or http_proxy URL verbatim, including embedded credentials, and then ignore it. The macOS 0.3.9 implementation refuses to start before model loading when either value lacks a parsable host and port; it reports variable names only. Valid inherited proxy settings remain active, including the TLS-inspection trust boundary
network_calls.data_sent: Standard HTTPS request metadata; no dictation audio. macOS 0.3.8 can attach an inherited HF_TOKEN, HUGGING_FACE_HUB_TOKEN, or HUGGINGFACEHUB_API_TOKEN as an Authorization header. Upcoming 0.3.9 removes those credentials from its own process before FluidAudio can read them, so its public model download carries no account credential; this does not alter the user's shell or token store. Both versions use the pinned FluidAudio client, which honors inherited lowercase https_proxy and http_proxy settings. A tunnelling proxy sees connection metadata but not request headers; a TLS-inspecting HTTPS proxy trusted by macOS could read any token sent by published 0.3.8. Upcoming 0.3.9 still honors proxy settings but removes inherited account-token authentication

network_calls.name: windows_first_launch_model_download
network_calls.when: Published Windows 0.1.12 starts its selected model download on first launch. Upcoming 0.1.13 checks the first-run default model cache locally and asks in Setup before downloading missing files for either default: English-only CPU base.en (~141 MiB) or Parakeet (~2.5 GB). Cached models load without a prompt; later Settings selections may also download missing files
destination: Hugging Face model-storage and CDN hosts under hf.co
Windows 0.1.12 only: inherited HF_ENDPOINT (if set) or the Hugging Face staging endpoint selected by HUGGINGFACE_CO_STAGING
Windows 0.1.12 only: configured Hub endpoint + /api/agent-harnesses when the local agent-registry cache is missing or stale
Windows 0.1.12 and 0.1.13: inherited HTTP_PROXY, HTTPS_PROXY, ALL_PROXY, and NO_PROXY settings can route model requests through a configured proxy
network_calls.purpose: Download local speech-model weights: multilingual Parakeet TDT v3 when NVIDIA CUDA is usable, or English-only Whisper base.en for the CPU first-run path; other models are user-selectable
network_calls.approximate_size: About 2.5 GB for a full Parakeet TDT v3 snapshot (a partial cache may need less) or 141 MiB for Whisper base.en
network_calls.data_sent: HTTPS request metadata, selected public model and revision, and bundled library/runtime versions in User-Agent fields; no dictation audio or transcript. Under defaults, Hugging Face observes and can count the model fetch itself. Published Windows 0.1.12 honors inherited HF_ENDPOINT and HUGGINGFACE_CO_STAGING settings, so a configured endpoint or the Hugging Face staging host can change the request destination; an available token may accompany a request to that destination. If HF_HUB_USER_AGENT_ORIGIN is set, the bundled client adds its value to User-Agent metadata. Published Windows 0.1.12 does not disable Hugging Face Hub/Transformers default usage telemetry, which these libraries may send; Transformers also includes a random per-process session identifier in model-request metadata. Exact Hub/Transformers telemetry event fields are defined by the bundled libraries and are not independently enumerated here. In pinned Hub 1.29.0, request-header construction may issue a best-effort GET to the configured endpoint /api/agent-harnesses when its local registry cache is missing or stale; it caches the response locally. Inherited agent-related environment markers may cause an agent/<id> label to be included in model-request User-Agent metadata. Upcoming Windows 0.1.13 disables Hub telemetry before imports and its packaged runtime rejects headers with agent attribution; these controls are not in published 0.1.12. Published Windows 0.1.12 also leaves implicit authentication enabled: if HF_TOKEN or HUGGING_FACE_HUB_TOKEN is available in the environment, or a token is saved in the local Hugging Face cache, a model request may include it. These public models do not require an account token. The release source pins hf-xet 1.6.0, whose upstream source predates the separately documented Xet client-transfer telemetry; 0.1.12 is not claimed to send those Xet reports. Upcoming Windows 0.1.13 forces the public huggingface.co endpoint, clears staging and inherited User-Agent-origin settings, disables Hub telemetry and implicit authentication, explicitly declines account tokens, and replaces Transformers' random request session ID with the fixed non-unique value telemetry-off. It bypasses the separate hf-xet transfer client through a runtime-checked Hub setting, preventing transfer telemetry in versions that implement it while retaining regular HTTP model downloads. These additional controls are not claimed for published 0.1.12. Both published Windows 0.1.12 and upcoming Windows 0.1.13 use the pinned Hugging Face Hub 1.29.0 HTTPX client (HTTPX 0.28.1) with its default trust_env=True. It honors inherited HTTP_PROXY, HTTPS_PROXY, ALL_PROXY, and NO_PROXY routing, plus SSL_CERT_FILE and SSL_CERT_DIR CA overrides; upcoming Windows 0.1.13 does not clear these proxy or CA settings. A proxy that only tunnels HTTPS sees connection metadata, not request contents. A TLS-inspecting HTTPS proxy whose CA is trusted by the client can read request headers and any account token sent by published Windows 0.1.12. Upcoming Windows 0.1.13 disables account-token authentication but still uses the configured proxy and CA settings. Published Windows 0.1.12 does not independently verify model-file contents against SHA-256. Upcoming Windows 0.1.13 verifies every allowed required and present optional inference file against a SHA-256 manifest tied to its pinned repository revision before model loading. On Windows, Presspeech rehashes the reviewed files on every load rather than trusting a metadata-only verification record; mismatches fail closed. This may lengthen model preparation. The proxy can still observe model-request metadata or block a download.

network_calls.name: macos_update_check
network_calls.when: Every 6 hours when automatic update checks are enabled, plus one check shortly after launch
network_calls.purpose: Check whether a newer immutable Presspeech release is available and notify the user
network_calls.data_sent: GET with a fixed User-Agent header, exactly presspeech-update-check; Presspeech adds no version, device, or user identifier and sends no transcript, microphone audio, settings, or usage counts. GitHub can observe the source IP address and request timing as ordinary connection metadata

network_calls.name: windows_update_check
network_calls.when: When the Windows app starts with automatic checks enabled and the recorded check is at least 24 hours old, plus manual checks from the tray menu. Published 0.1.12 records only successful checks, so a failed check can repeat on every restart. Upcoming 0.1.13 records automatic attempts before contacting GitHub, so failures also defer automatic retries for 24 hours. Manual retries remain available
network_calls.destination: api.github.com/repos/rcourtman/presspeech/releases?per_page=100, followed by bounded numbered pages from that same endpoint only when GitHub reports more than 100 releases
network_calls.purpose: Find a newer complete, immutable windows-vX.Y.Z release and offer it to the user
network_calls.data_sent: GET with a fixed User-Agent header, exactly presspeech-windows-update-check; Presspeech adds no version, device, or user identifier and sends no transcript, microphone audio, settings, or usage counts. GitHub or a configured proxy can observe connection metadata such as source IP address and request timing; GitHub sees the proxy's address when one is used
network_calls.proxy_routing: The Windows in-app updater uses Python urllib.request.ProxyHandler. It honors inherited https_proxy/HTTPS_PROXY and no_proxy/NO_PROXY settings and, when no environment proxy is set, Windows Internet Settings. A proxy for HTTPS requests can carry the automatic or manual release check. A CONNECT-only proxy sees connection metadata but not the HTTPS path or headers. A trusted TLS-inspecting proxy can read or change the response; the updater does not independently verify GitHub's release attestation. This is separate from the model client's HTTPX proxy and CA settings.

network_calls.name: user_triggered_support_guide
network_calls.when: Only when the user chooses Report a Problem or Suggest an Improvement
network_calls.purpose: Open the public support guide in the default browser; the app does not submit a report or attach diagnostics
network_calls.data_sent: The app adds no version, device, settings, transcript, diagnostics, or usage data to the fixed guide URL; the browser and GitHub handle normal request and account metadata. The user may separately follow an issue link from the guide when GitHub accepts submissions

network_calls.name: user_triggered_compatibility_guide
network_calls.when: In macOS 0.3.8, upcoming Windows 0.1.13, or builds containing the new action, and only when the user chooses Test App Compatibility
network_calls.purpose: Open the public privacy-safe repeated target-app test guide in the default browser
network_calls.data_sent: The app adds no version, device, settings, transcript, diagnostics, or usage data to the fixed URL; the browser and destination host handle normal request metadata

network_calls.name: user_triggered_install_or_update
network_calls.when: Only when the user downloads the app directly, installs through Homebrew, or chooses to update through the menu or Homebrew
network_calls.purpose: User-triggered install/update flow: immutable GitHub release download checked against its published SHA-256, a Homebrew metadata refresh followed by the signed macOS archive, or a Windows installer whose immutable release state, published size, and SHA-256 are verified before launch
network_calls.data_sent: Browser or Homebrew request metadata for those routes; the Windows in-app updater sends a fixed User-Agent and no dictation audio, transcript, device ID, or settings during the user-approved installer and checksum download. Its configured proxy can observe connection metadata. A trusted TLS-inspecting proxy can read or change GitHub responses; published size and SHA-256 checks only prove consistency with the release metadata received by this client, not an independently verified publisher signature.
network_calls.proxy_routing: Windows in-app installer and checksum downloads use Python urllib.request.ProxyHandler with inherited https_proxy/HTTPS_PROXY and no_proxy/NO_PROXY settings or, absent environment proxy settings, Windows Internet Settings. Each redirect URL must remain on an approved HTTPS GitHub asset host; these URL checks do not authenticate a TLS-inspecting proxy. Browser, Homebrew, and macOS routes follow their own proxy configuration.

local_storage.windows_model_integrity_cache: %LOCALAPPDATA%\Presspeech\model-integrity\ (local file-identity records after SHA-256 verification; no model or transcript content)
local_storage.transcripts: macOS recent transcript history is configurable, stays in memory only, and clears on quit; Windows does not keep an in-app transcript history
local_storage.clipboard: On macOS, pasted transcripts stay on the current pasteboard for automatic or manual paste. macOS 0.3.8 can expose transcript entries to macOS Universal Clipboard. Builds containing local-only transcript clipboard writes prepare every automatic-paste, recovery, recent-transcript and scratchpad copy as current-device-only and add standard transient, auto-generated, and concealed markers asking cooperating clipboard managers not to archive or visibly expose those entries while preserving local Command-V. Optional guarded restoration keeps an eligible complete previous clipboard only in memory; snapshots are limited to 64 MB and 256 representations and are skipped if incomplete, over either limit, or superseded by newer copied content. A restored previous clipboard retains its item representations but is republished current-device-only because the snapshot cannot recover its earlier cross-device scope. Apple's Screen Sharing has a separate shared-clipboard option that can transfer copied text between Macs; current-device-only transcript writes are not a tested guarantee against that feature. macOS Clipboard History in Spotlight on macOS 26 or later, Third-party clipboard managers that ignore those advisory markers, and other local readers remain separate boundaries. On Windows, the transcript remains on the current clipboard until overwritten. Published Windows 0.1.12 writes can enter Windows Clipboard History or Cloud Clipboard. Upcoming 0.1.13 places ExcludeClipboardContentFromMonitorProcessing on every dictation clipboard item before transcript text, instructing Windows not to retain or sync it through those services while preserving Ctrl+V. Microsoft Remote Desktop can redirect local clipboard text to a remote host when client and host policy permit; Moonlight can type local clipboard text into a remote host through its client-side shortcut. Windows Clipboard History and Cloud Clipboard exclusions do not establish what either remote client does. Presspeech does not provide a transcript-sync service.
